intro: I work across AI engineering and data analytics, with a focus on turning complex workflows into reliable systems. I'm currently an AI Engineering Intern at OriLoan Financial Inc.

I work end to end: cleaning the data, modeling the problem, and shipping it as something measurable and dependable. I learn fastest by building, validating against ground truth, and iterating on what the results reveal.
I'm currently open to internship and full-time opportunities where execution and continuous improvement matter.

roles.title: Intern – AI Engineer
bullets: Engineered an automated pricing ingestion and reconciliation platform covering 6 mortgage lenders across 5 heterogeneous portal architectures (REST API, replayable HTTP, ASP.NET WebForms, Blazor/SignalR, JSF), replacing manual rate sheet processing with a workflow that validated quotes against each lender’s official pricing engine.

Reverse-engineered the lender’s undocumented pricing rules into a deterministic model with no fitted parameters, raising pricing accuracy from 44.6% to 100% across 12,000 tested rate points and resolving a key blocker to launching a consumer rate product.

Implemented k-fold cross-validation across pricing scenarios and gated all 6 lenders in automated CI regression, ensuring pricing accuracy is continuously verified and protected from production regressions.

Hardened a public pricing API with rate limits for each caller, input validation and CloudWatch monitoring. Accelerated delivery by directing AI coding agents to build importers, run pricing sweeps at scale and analyze residuals.

roles.title: Intern – Front Office Operations
bullets: Identified a customer flow bottleneck through on site observation and frontline traffic monitoring, then recommended a queue redesign that streamlined lobby movement and reduced average wait times by 15% during peak hours.

Managed and triaged 50+ daily customer requests in a high volume environment, evaluated request trends by category to reveal recurring demand patterns, and informed desk level staffing allocation to strengthen coverage during busy periods.

Reviewed customer documentation and transaction records with close attention to detail, ensuring compliance with processing standards, minimizing downstream errors, and contributing to more consistent operational execution.

competition.title: America's Innovate IT Collegiate Conference (AITCC) — Analyze IT Challenge | 2nd Place
bullets: Joined and cleaned three relational tables (70K borrowers, 180K loans, 627K payment records) in Python, handling missing values, duplicates, orphaned foreign keys, and inconsistent formatting to produce a single loan-level modeling dataset.

Engineered payment behavior features from monthly repayment records including on-time rate, delinquency rate, and cumulative delinquent days. In exploratory analysis, payment behavior showed stronger associations with default than credit score or income.

Built models for default classification and days-to-default regression, achieving an AUC of 0.96 and an R² of 0.79 in the competition evaluation. Delivered a 12-slide visual report with risk monitoring recommendations.
